name: FAR.AI (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: an AI catastrophe kills people everywhere and the future lost is everyone's, so the result is spread by world population.
summary: FAR.AI (Berkeley and San Diego) works to make advanced AI safe: technical research on adversarial robustness, jailbreaks and red-teaming of frontier models, a research hub and coworking space in Berkeley, the Alignment Workshops and the International Dialogues on AI Safety, and research grants. This model covers all four programmes in 2024 ($8.6M spent). At the defaults it averts about {{result}} years of healthy life per $1,000, from {{low}} to {{high}} on its plausible range: each dollar is valued as a typical project's cut in the forecast risk of an AI catastrophe (Rethink Priorities' cross-cause model, the Existential Risk Persuasion Tournament's experts), with deaths valued like every death and the future lost counted only where you count lives that never start (0% by default). Over a quarter of its work (jailbreak research, red-teaming of safeguards and a grant for AI security research) is against misuse, for which Rethink's typical project cuts the deaths in catastrophes the world survives about 450 times more per dollar than misalignment work; that cut, the chance of an AI catastrophe (the slider) and the years a cut counts are the biggest swings. The next dollar counts at a fifth of the past average: reserves are large and the grants run on a restricted grant. Every branch is discounted for missing data: no outcome of the work on the risk is measured.

rows.label: AI: share of the AI spending on work against misuse (dangerous-capability evaluations, defences against misuse)
rows.explainer: The share of FAR.AI's AI spending that is work against misuse. Of its 12 papers of 2024 (far.ai/publications), two are misuse work (jailbreak-tuning and data poisoning that strip a model's refusals; how robustness against jailbreaks scales with compute); the other ten are interpretability, reward misspecification, the robustness of superhuman Go AIs and guaranteed safe AI, aimed at AI that doesn't do what its makers intend. With the red-teaming of frontier systems' safeguards (990 Part III line 4a), also misuse work, about a third of research ($0.99M). The $1.46M grant went to one European organisation (Schedule F); the one European project on FAR.AI's grants list, ETH Zurich's 'Failure Modes in Superhuman Systems', covers data poisoning, consistency checks, model stealing and prompt injection, three of the four against attackers, so three quarters ($1.10M). None of the workshops, the dialogues or the hub, whose topics are mostly alignment and governance. About $2.08M of $7.52M, 28%, our judgment; 11% (research by papers alone, the grant a quarter) to 40% (research half, the grant all). Work aimed at both counts as misalignment.

rows.label: AI: years from the spending until the work cuts the risk
rows.explainer: From the year's spending to its effect on the risk. Reference class: flaws reported to software developers are fixed within a 90-day disclosure window (Google Project Zero's policy), while laws act later: the EU AI Act, adopted in 2024, applies in full 24 months after it enters into force (European Parliament, 13 March 2024). FAR.AI's work spans both: red-teaming findings reach the labs' safeguards within months, papers and workshops change what others build over a year or two, and the dialogues' proposals act only once governments do. Our judgment 1.5 years (0.5 to 4); discounted at the shared rate.

source.quote: If a vendor patches a security issue 47 days after Project Zero notifies the vendor about the vulnerability, details will be made public on day 90.

rows.formula: -((cost_total * ai_cost_share / 1e6 * ai_future_per_million * ai_discounted_years) + (cost_total * bio_cost_share / 1e6 * bio_future_per_million * bio_discounted_years) + (cost_total * nuclear_cost_share / 1e6 * nuclear_future_per_million * nuclear_discounted_years) + (pol_wins * pol_p_success * pol_relative_cut * pol_future_per_year * pol_discounted_years) + (fb_work_dollars / 1e6 * fb_credit_share * fb_future_per_million * pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, years_of_impact))) * $lives_added * $animal_dalys_per_person_year_world
rows.explainer: A future kept is also every animal raised to feed it: each future person-year at the suffering of the animals an average person eats in a year today (docs/normalization.md 2.25). Suffering always counts, whatever lives that never start count; the farmed animals' own good days count where you set them to. Held at today's diet: no forecast of what people will eat is used.

rows.explainer: FAR.AI's research against Rethink Priorities' typical small AI project. Above typical: its papers are accepted at the main machine-learning venues, its attacks on frontier models' safeguards reach the developers (in 2025 OpenAI's GPT-5 system card reports FAR.AI's red-teaming of its safeguards and says OpenAI is acting on some of the weaknesses found; that work is 2025's, a sign of the uptake, not counted here), and the 990 reports red-teaming engagements on frontier systems and work with government AI security initiatives in 2024. Below in how directly it acts: showing a weakness cuts the risk only once developers fix it. 1.2, our judgment, 0.4 to 2.5.

rows.label: Research hub: how far the typical project's effect applies
rows.explainer: A dollar of FAR.Labs against a typical small AI project's dollar. The members' research is paid by their own employers and grants; the hub's dollar buys desks, seminars and the chance meetings that speed their work and help new organisations start. Below typical: the Bay Area has other AI safety hubs (Constellation, Lighthaven), so much of the members' work would go on nearly as well elsewhere. 0.6, our judgment, 0.2 to 1.2, lower still because the hub supports work rather than doing it.

rows.label: Events: how far the typical project's effect applies
rows.explainer: FAR.AI's events against a typical small AI project. The Alignment Workshops (its largest yet in 2024) bring together researchers from the frontier labs, universities and governments; the International Dialogues on AI Safety gave scientists from China and the West (Bengio, Hinton, Yao) a joint statement calling for emergency-preparedness agreements, one of very few channels of its kind. Neither acts directly on the risk: workshops change what attendees do, the statements act only through governments. 1, our judgment, 0.3 to 2.5, wide because the dialogues' effect on policy is unknown.

rows.explainer: How far Rethink Priorities' typical small AI project applies to FAR.AI's work: the four programmes weighted by their spending (990 Part III): about 1.02.

rows.label: Share of the work no one else would have done now
rows.explainer: The share of the work no one else would have done now: academic groups and the labs themselves study adversarial robustness and red-team models, the UK and US AI safety institutes test safeguards, and other Bay Area hubs and conferences exist; the Go and jailbreak-tuning attacks, the largest alignment-focused workshops and an East-West scientists' dialogue are close to unique. Our judgment, 0.65 (0.35 to 0.85); that the work would have come later is in years_of_impact.

Our judgment, 0.85 (0.65 to 1).

rows.label: This charity's share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.explainer: FAR.AI's share of all resources behind its work: the share of its own spending not paid by fees (earned_revenue), times its share against outside contributors (partner_share): about 0.81.

rows.label: This charity's share of the good done with money, work or budgets it brings in
rows.explainer: The site's one setting for resources another party commits only because of the organisation (docs/normalization.md 2.24): governments' budgets and enforcement, companies' compliance, the use others make of research. The charity is credited this share of the good done with them, net of their cost; the rest stays with those who paid or did the work. Fixed.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The share among co-advocates times the mobiliser's share: the rest of the credit stays with those who carry out the result (docs/normalization.md 2.24).

rows.label: Leverage and funging
rows.explainer: Whether large funders (Open Philanthropy, now Coefficient Giving, the Survival and Flourishing Fund, Schmidt Sciences) would give less if small donors gave more is the room factor of @next_dollar.far_ai (docs/normalization.md 2.10), so it isn't asked again here (one question per adjustment): 1, our judgment, as for every catastrophic-risk model; 0.85 to 1.05 for funging the room factor misses.

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: Thin: no outcome of FAR.AI's work on the risk is measured (papers, red-teaming reports and attendance are outputs); the cut per dollar is a typical project's from Rethink Priorities' model and the chances are forecasts, so the shared missing-data step applies (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above.

rows.label: Benefits not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Good beyond the catastrophes counted: robustness and red-teaming work also guards against harms smaller than a catastrophe (jailbroken models helping with fraud or abuse), the hub helped new organisations start, and the workshops' recordings reach people beyond the room. 10% (0 to 30%) of the modelled value, our judgment.

rows.label: Harm: speeding up dangerous capabilities, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Beyond a typical project's backfire (in the shared cut): adversarial training and robustness research also make AI systems more reliable, which helps the labs ship more capable products, and the hub hosts some people from frontier labs. -3%, our judgment, down to -15%, small because FAR.AI builds no capability benchmark the labs race on.

rows.label: Harm: information hazards and attention, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Beyond a typical project's backfire: FAR.AI publishes new attacks (jailbreak-tuning strips a fine-tunable model's refusals in a morning's work), which teach misusers as well as defenders; the fine-tuning attacks need access the developers can close. -5%, down to -20%, our judgment, because these are working attacks.
